nodes.description: Two damaged copies of NFS1, the gene encoding the mitochondrial cysteine desulfurase. NFS1 is a pyridoxal-5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme that abstracts sulfur from L-cysteine as a persulfide and feeds it into the ISC assembly pathway, acting as part of a core complex with its partner ISD11 (LYRM4), the scaffold ISCU and ferredoxin. The recurrent p.Arg72Gln substitution lies in the conserved aminotransferase-class-V domain and destabilizes the protein: patient fibroblasts show markedly reduced NFS1 transcript and protein relative to controls, and the NFS1-ISD11 interaction is lost, so less sulfur is delivered for cluster synthesis. This is a quantitative (hypomorphic/loss-of-function) lesion rather than a change in a catalytic residue.

nodes.description: Respiratory-chain complexes I, II and III each require Fe-S clusters, so a shortfall in cluster supply reduces their activity together while the Fe-S-free complex IV is relatively spared - the biochemical pattern that names the disease. Patient muscle and liver show complex II and III deficiency (with variable complex I involvement), and both mitochondrial and cytosolic aconitase activities are reduced, reflecting the broader Fe-S enzyme dependence; lipoylation of pyruvate and 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase is only mildly affected.

The recurrent missense allele (c.215G>A), homozygous in all reported severe infantile cases and present on at least one allele in every published patient. It destabilizes NFS1, reducing its transcript and protein level. It has recurred in unrelated populations (Old Order Mennonite and Christian Arab) with no shared haplotype, so it behaves as a recurrent de novo hot-spot rather than a single founder allele.
